rounds.name: Online Assessment (MCQ Round)
rounds.description: Platform : HackerEarth. Eligibility: CE and CSE (For the 2025 passout batch, EXTC was also eligible, so for 2027, anything could happen.). There was a 7.5+ CGPA criteria to apply. There were 21 technical MCQs and 50 mins were given, but 15–20 mins were more than enough to complete everything.

rounds.name: Machine Coding Round
rounds.description: 7 candidates appeared for this round. Offline. 2hrs. It’s just a problem statement, and you need to provide a solution. BrowserStack has been using the same problem statement for the last 3-4 years. The problem involves implementing Socket.IO for real-time updates, so make sure you’re comfortable with it. We were called to BrowserStack’s office in Goregaon for the machine coding round and interview. HR called every selected candidate 2 days before the interview to invite us to their Goregaon office. On the call, she mentioned there would be 2 rounds: machine coding and then an interview. She also said the machine coding problem statement requires knowledge of Socket.IO and suggested practicing for the machine coding round. Candidates were divided into batches, with 5 candidates per batch and one mentor per batch. On the same day, there were candidates from other colleges too. I think there were about 12 batches in total. I was in Batch 1 with 5 candidates, all from our college. The other 2 candidates from our college were in Batch 2 with 3 candidates from a different college.

questions.text: Implement a log-watching solution (similar to the tail -f command in UNIX). The log file is hosted on a remote machine (same machine as your server code). The log file is in append-only mode. Implement a server-side program to monitor the given log file and stream updates as they happen using Socket.IO for real-time communication. Implement a web-based client (accessible via a URL like http://localhost/log) that displays updates in the file in real-time, without requiring a page refresh. The page should load once and keep updating. On initial load, the user should see the last 10 lines of the file.
The server must push updates to clients in real-time using Socket.IO.
The log file could be several GBs. How do you optimize retrieving the last 10 lines?
The server should not retransmit the entire file every time; it should only send updates.
The server must handle multiple clients simultaneously.
The web page should not stay in a loading state after the first load and should not reload thereafter.
You may not use off-the-shelf external libraries or tools to read the file or provide tail-like functionalities (except Socket.IO for real-time updates).
Browser automation without using automation frameworks.

rounds.name: Interview Round
rounds.description: 3 candidates appeared for this round. 50-55 min in my case. The interviewer was the Director of Engineering. He kicked things off by introducing himself and then asked about my CET, SSC, and HSC scores, and why I chose SPIT. After that, he asked me to give a quick introduction about myself. Then, he asked about my internship experience, specifically what I did during it and what kind of work I handled. I shared details about my role, the tasks I contributed to, and the impact I made, like leading development or solving specific challenges. Once I was done, he explained the interview flow: first, we’d dive into my projects, and then he’d test my problem-solving skills.

tips.text: They evaluate not just your MCQ score but also shortlist based on your resume, so ensure it highlights solid development skills.

Know every single line of your code and why you wrote it, as the mentor will ask about your logic and the reasoning behind specific lines, especially how you implemented Socket.IO for real-time updates.
OOPS: Study on GeeksforGeeks (GFG) Best Resource for OOPS.
Puzzles: Practice GFG’s Top 100 Puzzles.
SQL: Check Drive link PDF for overlooked SQL topics.
Project Architecture: Know your project’s design and choices.
Database Scaling & CAP Theorem: Understand scaling and trade-offs.
Rate Limiting: Learn API rate limiting basics.
Pagination: Study efficient data handling.
JWT Authentication: Know how JWT works for APIs.
JavaScript: Master Event Loop, Fetch API, debouncing, throttling.
Node.js Concurrency: Explain how single-threaded Node.js handles concurrency.
MVC Architecture: Understand Model-View-Controller basics.
React.js: Study Virtual DOM, state management, hooks, component lifecycle.
Java: Learn JDK, JRE, JVM flow, garbage collection, stack/heap memory.

rounds.name: Machine Coding Round
rounds.description:
It was conducted in Batches offline in the BrowserStack office in Oberoi Commerz 2. Due to the limited number of students they had confined a single batch for SPIT. The PS for the machine coding round is shared below: This problem requires you to implement a log-watching solution (similar to the tail -f command in UNIX). However, the log file is hosted on a remote machine (same machine as your server code). The log file is in append-only mode. You need to implement the following: A server-side program to monitor the given log file and stream updates as they happen using Socket.IO for real-time communication. This will run on the same machine as the log file. You can use any programming language for the server. A web-based client (accessible via a URL like http://localhost/log) that displays updates in the file in real-time, without requiring a page refresh. The page should load once and keep updating. On initial load, the user should see the last 10 lines of the file. Problem Constraints: The server must push updates to clients in real-time using Socket.IO. The log file could be several GBs. How do you optimize retrieving the last 10 lines? The server should not retransmit the entire file every time; it should only send updates. The server must handle multiple clients simultaneously. The web page should not stay in a loading state after the first load and should not reload thereafter. You may not use off-the-shelf external libraries or tools to read the file or provide tail-like functionalities (except Socket.IO for real-time updates). You’ll be evaluated on code quality, testability, modularity, and handling of corner cases. The Machine coding round began at 10:30 AM and we were given roughly 2 hrs to build the backend server. You may find the solutions online, but an optimal solution that caters to the edge cases of the invigilator is preferred. You are not allowed to use any AI agents or LLMs or medium articles during this round, our invigilator was right beside us. You may refer to the documentation for development. You can interact with the invigilator during the round. Primary goal is to develop the solution using Socket.IO , I preferred NODE for the backend and socket implementation to display logs realtime with a confined Buffer to prevent parsing the logs. The invigilator would test it on multiple edge cases, like real time parsing, multiple browser compatibility with realtime logs and order in which they appear or cases where ‘
’ appears while parsing logs. If it passes all the cases and you are able to explain your code really well then you would be moved forward to the next round.

rounds.name: Machine Coding Round
rounds.description: This problem requires you to implement a log watching solution (similar to the tail -f command in UNIX). However, in this case, the log file is hosted on a remote machine (same machine as your server code). The log file is in append-only mode. You may implement the server in any programming language. You have to implement the following: 1. A server side program to monitor the given log file and capable of streaming updates that happen in it. This will run on the same machine as the log file. 2. A web based client (accessible via URL like http://localhost/log) that prints the updates in the file as and when they happen and NOT upon page refresh. The page should be loaded once and it should keep getting updated in real-time. 3. The user sees the last 10 lines in the file when they visit the page for the first time. Problem Constraints: The server should push updates to the clients as we have to be as real time as possible. Do this by Websokets in node you can use socket.io. Be aware that the log file may be several GB, how to optimise for retrieving the last 10 lines – Use list of last 10 lines and updates it when file changes and read file in reverse and load small chunk in buffer instead of loading complete file. The server should not retransmit the entire file every time. It should only send the updates. – Create event update (to get new lines) init (to get last 10 lines). The server should be able to handle multiple clients at the same time. They will be evaluating you for working solution, code efficiency, corner cases, etc.

questions.text: Implement a log watching solution (similar to the tail -f command in UNIX). The log file is hosted on a remote machine (same machine as your server code) and is in append-only mode. Implement: 1. A server side program to monitor the given log file and capable of streaming updates. 2. A web based client (accessible via URL like http://localhost/log) that prints updates in real-time, not upon page refresh. 3. The user sees the last 10 lines when visiting the page for the first time. Constraints: Server pushes updates via WebSockets (e.g., socket.io). Optimize for retrieving last 10 lines of a multi-GB file (e.g., use a list of last 10 lines, read file in reverse, load small chunks). Server sends only updates, not entire file (e.g., 'update' event for new lines, 'init' for last 10 lines). Server handles multiple clients.

tips.text: Begin your placement preparation as early as possible. Focus on fundamental computer science subjects such as DBMS, Operating Systems, Computer Networks, and Object-Oriented Programming (OOPs). Make concise, revision-friendly notes for these subjects to help during the last-minute prep. Also, research frequently asked interview questions to become familiar with recurring patterns and concepts.

Your resume should reflect your actual knowledge and experience. Avoid adding skills or technologies that you cannot explain if asked in the interview it may come off as dishonest and create a negative impression. At the very least, ensure you understand the basic concepts of everything mentioned. Tailor your resume slightly depending on the specific role you're applying for.

The first step in most placement processes is usually a company presentation. Be attentive and note important details about the company’s history, products, services, and culture. If you have doubts about the roles and responsibilities, clarify them early. This will help you make an informed decision and also position yourself as someone who is genuinely interested in the company.

For Online Assessments (OAs), consistent practice can make a big difference. Participate in coding contests and take timed tests to improve your problem solving speed and accuracy. This will also help you identify your weak areas and improve over time.

In interviews, focus on explaining your approach clearly rather than jumping to give the right answer immediately. Interviewers are more interested in your thought process and problem-solving skills. Staying calm and confident shows that you can perform under pressure, which is an essential trait for any role.

Finally, don’t lose hope if things don’t go as planned. Focus on how you can improve your chances of getting selected. Understand your strengths and weaknesses, and keep refining them throughout the placement season. Persistence and continuous improvement are key.
